newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria consults neighbours on Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria consults neighbours on Sierra Leone.

text.p: Nigeria is consulting its West African neighbours on the situation in Liberia and Sierra Leone, state radio reported on Tuesday.
It said Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi, returning from a tour of some West African states, briefed military ruler General Sani Abacha in the capital Abuja on the outcome of his talks.

Ikimi went to Ghana, Guinea and Liberia and talked with Major-General Victor Malu, Nigerian commander of the West African peacekeeping force ECOMOG, which has troops stationed in Liberia and Sierra Leone.

Following a May 25 coup that ousted the elected president of Sierra Leone, Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, the Nigerian-led ECOMOG force has massed in Freetown with the stated aim of restoring democracy in the impoverished country.
Nigerian gunboats shelled Freetown on June 2 and Nigerian soldiers were in turn attacked by Sierra Leone forces and their rebel allies at a hotel where Nigerians were guarding foreigners.
Since then, a much expected Nigerian military intervention has not materialised despite a continued buildup of ECOMOG forces in Sierra Leone.
The new Sierra Leone military leader Johnny Paul Koroma was sworn in on Tuesday as head of state.
